topic: Decide which programming language to standardize on for a new service

scenario.topic: Decide which programming language to standardize on for a new service
scenario.opening_question: What matters most to you when picking a language: speed, developer experience, or ecosystem?

options.name: Go 1.20 with Standard Library
options.upside: Efficient concurrency and fast compile times
options.tradeoff: Limited third-party libraries compared to older languages
options.concern: May lack some advanced language features needed later

options.name: Python 3.11 with Asyncio Framework
options.tradeoff: Slower runtime performance and higher memory use
options.concern: May struggle under heavy concurrency workloads
options.best_for: rapid prototyping and rich library access

options.name: Rust 1.70 with Tokio Runtime
options.tradeoff: Steep learning curve and longer initial development time
options.concern: Smaller talent pool and fewer mature libraries

options.name: Node.js 18 with TypeScript
options.upside: Unified language for frontend and backend with rich packages
options.tradeoff: Single-threaded event loop can limit CPU-bound tasks
options.concern: Callback-heavy code can become complex without discipline
options.best_for: full-stack development with strong ecosystem support

shared_context: The team has exactly 2 members deciding together
The new service must be ready for production within 6 months
The budget allows for moderate training but prefers maintainability

personas.name: Tala
personas.background: As a systems engineer focused on performance and safety, I prioritize memory-safe and high-performance languages for critical services.
personas.private_goal: I want the team to adopt Rust 1.70 to ensure safe concurrency and top runtime performance despite the steeper learning curve.

agenda.reason: state one grounded reason for the initial preference
ask about a practical constraint that could affect the choice
compare the preferred option with a realistic alternative
object to the main rival option with a concrete concern

personas.name: Nadia
personas.background: As a product manager emphasizing rapid iteration and broad ecosystem support, I value fast prototyping and easy onboarding.
personas.private_goal: I want to standardize on Python 3.11 to leverage its vast libraries and very fast development speed for quick feature delivery.

agenda.reason: state one grounded reason for the initial preference
ask about a practical constraint that could affect the choice
compare the preferred option with a realistic alternative
look for a workable compromise the group could accept
